function: Learned (PPO) transmit power and subchannel allocation, plus a handover indicator, per beam in a multibeam LEO satellite system; beam activation uses a non-learned heuristic (pp. 6-9).
system: Multibeam LEO constellation (780 km, 11 satellites x 6 planes), phased-array Ka-band beams, up to 12 beams per satellite, ground users; no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: PPO actor-critic reinforcement learning (two-layer perceptrons, Gaussian power and Bernoulli subchannel policies), trained 300 epochs in simulation; beam hopping by non-learned P-center clustering (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: free-space path loss, Bessel-function beam gain, ITU-R rain and cloud attenuation, complex Gaussian fast fading, Poisson-distributed users; no 3GPP model or measured data (pp. 4-5, 9).
test_conditions: DRL trained 300 epochs (batch 300) and evaluated through training curves in the same simulator, for uniform and non-uniform users; no separate test set (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Beam-hopping clustering only: K-means, K-means++, Max-Dur, Min-Dis, Max-SNR (non-learned). No baseline, learned or not, for the PPO power and subchannel allocation (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Average beam throughput utility, hop count for full coverage, coverage efficiency, PPO total reward, beam SINR, transmit power and gain, EPFD versus ITU limit (pp. 10-11).
complexity: PPO online O(I+BtK+UK) per slot, training O(SI) per batch, epoch O(SI+S(BtK+UK)); clustering O(BtU log U) versus O(U^3) exact (pp. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 5: "Leading to a free-space path loss [48]"; Table I (p. 9) lists free space path loss, complex Gaussian fast fading with variance 1, and ITU-R rain and cloud models. It is a custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.811 model or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "The DRL agent is trained over 300 epochs with a batch size of 300"; p. 10: "for uniform distribution, the reward curve exhibits a steady monotonic increase with minimal oscillations". Figs. 5-8 are training curves; no trained policy is tested on a scenario outside training.
q3_support: p. 10: "The proposed refined P-center algorithm is compared with traditional K-means and K-means++", which are non-learned and concern the beam clustering only. Section IV-C (pp. 10-11, Figs. 5-8) shows only the PPO's own curves; no earlier learned method (DQN, DDPG, other DRL) is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "the worst-case online complexity is O(I + Bt K + U K)"; the same paragraph gives O(SI) for each PPO training batch, and p. 7 gives O(Bt U log U) for the clustering heuristic.
q5_support: p. 9: "The proposed framework is evaluated under a multibeam LEO satellite system with parameters listed in Table I". All data are simulated; no link to code or data appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 6: the PPO agent controls transmit power and subchannel assignment (and a handover indicator) in a multibeam LEO link; beam activation is a non-learned heuristic (Algorithm 1, p. 8), so the learned decision is physical layer and the handover decision is admitted jointly. The paper describes the actor outputs inconsistently: Section II-E (p. 6) lists beam activation, power and handover with subchannels by heuristic, while Section III-B and Algorithm 2 (pp. 8-9) learn subchannel assignment and power. The ITU-R P.341-7 and P.840-8 models are used only for the attenuation factor (Table I, p. 9), so q1 is 0; the reviewer may confirm. The abstract claims superiority over conventional static allocation, but no such baseline appears in Figs. 3-8. Table I and Figs. 3-8 were read from the page images (pp. 9-11).
